entries.note: Lemon posset = Lemon shell (crème)
entries.definition: A British dessert of cream, sugar and lemon juice set into a soft, tangy custard, often served in a small glass or shell (une crème au citron).
entries.example: After the raclette, Maman served a lemon posset in tiny glasses, and even Auryn asked for seconds.

entries.key: we ve run out of milk
entries.note: We’ve run out of milk
entries.definition: To use up the whole supply of something so that none is left.
entries.example: We've run out of milk, so I'll pop to the shop before the children wake up.

entries.key: taken up medication to help manage
entries.note: She has taken up medication to help manage her stress level
entries.definition: To start taking a course of medicine regularly, here to help control a condition such as stress.
entries.example: She has taken up medication to help manage her stress level.

entries.note: I feel ghastly (sick or super tired)
entries.definition: To feel very ill or extremely tired, in a way that is thoroughly unpleasant.
entries.example: I feel ghastly this morning, so I think I'll stay in bed after marking those essays.

entries.note: I have to catch up on sleep
entries.definition: To sleep extra hours to make up for earlier nights when you did not get enough rest.
entries.example: I have to catch up on sleep this weekend after a week of late nights.

entries.note: Sleep, Creep, Leap (1st, 2nd and 3rd years for a plant)
entries.definition: A gardeners' saying for how a perennial plant grows: it sleeps in its first year, creeps in its second and leaps in its third.
entries.example: Be patient with the new lavender, because the saying goes sleep, creep, leap over three years.

entries.note: Many people find sanctuary in nature.
entries.definition: To find a place or thing that gives you safety, peace and relief from worry.
entries.example: Many people find sanctuary in nature.

entries.note: Talking with Preeti was the stimulus in my choice of studies
entries.definition: Something that prompts or encourages an action, a development or a decision.
entries.example: Talking with Preeti was the stimulus in my choice of studies.

entries.note: Abbreviations for DM NP (no problem), IM(H)O (in my honest opinion), TBD (to be decided), TBC (to be confirmed), TBH (to be honest)
entries.definition: An abbreviation of "to be confirmed", used in messages for details that are not yet certain; others in her list include NP, IMHO, TBD and TBH.
entries.example: The date of the school trip to the Vercors is still TBC, so I'll text you later.

entries.note: What’s the catch?!
entries.definition: A hidden problem or disadvantage in something that seems too good to be true.
entries.example: The holiday cottage costs almost nothing, so what's the catch?

entries.theme: Efficiency & work + at work + with students
entries.note: I’m going to power on through
entries.definition: To keep going with determination and energy despite difficulty, tiredness or obstacles until a task is finished.
entries.example: I'm going to power on through and finish marking these essays before the students arrive tomorrow.

entries.note: Her ideas are taking us into a blind alley…
entries.definition: A course of action or line of thought that leads nowhere and offers no chance of progress.
entries.example: Her ideas are taking us into a blind alley, so we should rethink the whole lesson plan.

entries.note: to be a third/fifth wheel
entries.definition: To be an unwanted extra person who feels in the way when two others, usually a couple, are together.
entries.example: I didn't want to be a third wheel, so I let Ella and her friend go skiing alone.

entries.note: We will probably just hangout; you’re working too hard why don’t you take a breather and meet me for coffee?
entries.definition: To stop what you are doing for a short rest before carrying on.
entries.example: You're working too hard, so why don't you take a breather and meet me for coffee?

entries.key: don t make a fuss it s just a small mistake
entries.note: Don’t make a fuss—it’s just a small mistake.
entries.definition: To show too much worry, annoyance or excitement about something unimportant.
entries.example: Don't make a fuss, it's just a small mistake and we can easily put it right.

entries.note: That is a bargain!
entries.definition: Something bought for much less than its usual or real value.
entries.example: That coat is a bargain; I found it in the sales in Grenoble for half price.

entries.key: i had to step over the mess to reach the alexandre iii bridge spans the seine
entries.note: I had to step over the mess to reach… / The Alexandre III Bridge spans the Seine
entries.definition: A dirty or untidy state of things, or a place where things are scattered in disorder.
entries.example: I had to step over the mess of toys on the floor to reach Auryn's bedroom.

entries.key: as a canary in a coal mine an early warning of danger or failure
entries.term: a canary in a coal mine
entries.note: As a canary in a coal mine = an early warning of danger or failure
entries.definition: Something or someone whose condition gives an early warning of danger or failure.
entries.example: Falling attendance in the morning classes could be a canary in a coal mine for the whole course.

entries.key: it is a very unusual day all around
entries.note: It is a very unusual day all around
entries.definition: Different from what is normal or expected; strange or remarkable.
entries.example: It is a very unusual day all around, with snow falling on the Alps in late May.

entries.note: Embezzlement = détournements de fonds
entries.definition: The crime of secretly taking money that has been entrusted to you, especially from an employer (détournement de fonds).
entries.example: The treasurer was jailed for embezzlement after money vanished from the school's trip fund.
